text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's composition proves nothing on its own. All-women panels are unremarkable in education, where women dominate the workforce, and panels routinely appoint candidates of the opposite sex. Leading with it makes you look aggrieved rather than wronged, and it's the easiest part of your case to dismiss.

Your real argument is substantive: on the stated leadership criteria you appear better qualified — a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing the deputy's job versus unspecified "courses." That's a comparison a tribunal or ombudsman can evaluate.

Also pursue the unanswered request. In most jurisdictions you're entitled to written reasons, and an unexplained delay is itself a procedural failing. Send a dated follow-up, cite the relevant provision, and keep records.
